title: Clinical Laboratory Rates Updated Effective July 1, 2026
agency: California Department of Health Care Services / Medi-Cal
summary: Effective for dates of service on or after July 1, 2026, the reimbursement rates for certain clinical laboratory services have been updated. The updated rates are available on the Medi-Cal Rates page of the Medi-Cal Providers website. An Erroneous Payment Correction (EPC) will be implemented to reprocess claims with dates of service on or after the effective date of this billing policy, that were appropriately submitted based on the guidance published in this article but erroneously reimbursed because Medi-Cal had not yet implemented the system changes to support appropriate adjudication. Providers may also elect to use this updated billing policy to correct and resubmit previously denied claims as described in the CIF Submission and Timeliness Instructions section of the Provider Manual. Background Welfare and Institutions Code (W&I Code), Section 14105.22 requires that reimbursement rates for clinical laboratory or laboratory services are the lowest of several factors, including 100 percent of the lowest maximum allowance established by the federal Medicare program for the same or similar service. title: Important Reminder: Ordering, Referring and Prescribing (ORP) Enrollment Requirements
agency: California Department of Health Care Services / Medi-Cal
summary: Per the Center for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) mandate, providers that bill for goods and/or services ordered, referred or prescribed by another provider are required to list the National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the provider who ordered, referred or prescribed the goods or services being billed on the Medi-Cal claim. The ordering, referring and prescribing (ORP) provider must be enrolled as a participating provider in Medi-Cal and Type 1 (Individual) NPI even if the provider does not send claims directly to Medi-Cal for the goods or services they furnish. Medi-Cal providers are strongly encouraged to share this information and work directly with their unenrolled ORP providers to take proactive action and submit a provider enrollment application through the Department of Health Care Services’ (DHCS’) Provider Application and Validation for Enrollment portal to enroll with their Type 1 (Individual) NPI. Note : Providers and billers can check the Profile of Enrolled Medi-Cal Fee-for-Service (FFS) Providers web page on the California Health and Human Services Open Data Portal website to verify enrollment. A taxonomy code is a unique 10-character code established/maintained by the National Uniform Claims Committee (NUCC) that designates a provider’s grouping, classification and area of specialization. Providers may validate the taxonomy code associated with their NPI and practice location through the Provider Application and Validation for Enrollment (PAVE) Portal . If a provider is associated with more than one taxonomy code, the provider must submit the taxonomy code that most accurately corresponds/describes the group and specialty classification of the service rendered. DHCS may implement a reimbursement methodology which uses taxonomy codes in the future. Providers are encouraged to include taxonomy codes on their claims to avoid delays in processing. title: Reminder: Use the Provider Manual for Current Billing Instructions for HCPCS Codes J3392 and J3394
agency: California Department of Health Care Services / Medi-Cal
summary: The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) is reminding providers that the most current billing instructions for HCPCS codes J3392 (injection, exagamglogene autotemcel, per treatment) (Casgevy) and J3394 (injection, lovotibeglogene autotemcel, per treatment) (Lyfgenia) are available in the Medi‑Cal Provider Manual. Older Quarterly HCPCS Policy Update PDFs may contain outdated clinical criteria or billing information and should not be used. Both codes are a part of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Cell and Gene Therapy (CGT) Access Model. Guidance on the CGT Access Model and the latest billing instructions for both codes are available in the following provider manual sections: Cell and Gene Therapy CMS Cell and Gene Therapy Access Model For additional resources, providers can refer to the Cell and Gene Therapy Access Model web page on the DHCS website, which includes Frequently Asked Question documents. For federal program requirements, providers can visit the CGT (Cell and Gene Therapy Access) Model web page on the CMS website. Using these resources ensures accurate and current billing for HCPCS codes J3392 and J3394.

title: Remittance Advice Detail Code 010: Denials for Duplicate Claims
agency: California Department of Health Care Services / Medi-Cal
summary: A frequent cause of claim denials by Medi-Cal is due to incorrect recipient admission and discharge dates and/or incorrect patient status codes submitted by providers. Erroneous “from-through” dates or patient status billed by one provider and paid by Medi-Cal can result in the denial of correct claims billed by another provider. This often occurs between hospitals and nursing homes during the transfer of the recipient. Providers see this on their Remittance Advice Details (RADs) as a claim denied by RAD code 010. Should the denied provider choose to dispute the claim and there is no resolution between the two providers regarding the dates in question, Medi-Cal could recoup the full reimbursement of the original erroneously paid claim, and will not make an adjustment without a correction request from that provider. Incorrectly paid and denied claims can also create incorrect provider reimbursement data and inaccuracies in the health service records that may impact beneficiary share of cost, access to services and estate recovery. The changes were made as a result of extensive engagement with key stakeholders. Specifically, DHCS has updated the Treatment Authorization Request (TAR) monetary threshold for the purchase price of all DME codes and for the repair, maintenance or replacement part cost of wheelchair group HCPCS codes. Moreover, HCPCS code K0462 (temporary replacement for patient-owned equipment being repaired, any type) has been updated from a non-standard benefit to a benefit, which is intended to ensure Medi-Cal members have access to a temporary replacement wheelchair while their primary wheelchair is inaccessible due to repairs or maintenance. title: Responsible County and Residence County Clarified in Provider Manual
agency: California Department of Health Care Services / Medi-Cal
summary: The Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) has clarified the definitions of residence counties and responsible counties in the provider manual. The responsible county, or county of responsibility, is the county that is responsible for determining a Medi-Cal member’s eligibility. The residence county, or county of residence, is the county that the Medi-Cal member reports they currently reside in. A member’s residence county and responsible county will be visible on responses from the Medi-Cal eligibility verification system. A member’s responsible county may not be the same as the residence county. Billing Instructions If the member is enrolled in a Dental MCP at the time services are rendered, clinics must bill the member’s assigned Dental MCP for reimbursement at the AIR. If the member is enrolled in a Dental MCP and receives both medical health and oral health services on the same day, submit the claim for medical health services to the Medi-Cal Managed Care Plan or Medi-Cal fee-for-service. If the member is not enrolled in a Dental MCP at the time services are rendered and is enrolled in Medi-Cal Dental fee-for-service, submit the claim to Medi-Cal Dental fee-for-service.
